stem: A 4-year-old boy is being toilet trained. His micturition reflex, triggered when bladder stretch receptors signal the sacral spinal cord, produces voiding through which of the following effector responses?

options.label: A
options.text: Sympathetic outflow contracts the detrusor and closes the external sphincter
options.misconception: The filling-phase autonomic pattern is being applied to voiding.
options.explanation: Sympathetic activity via the hypogastric nerves suppresses detrusor contraction during filling; voiding is a parasympathetic event with sphincter relaxation.

options.label: B
options.text: Parasympathetic outflow contracts the detrusor, relaxing the internal sphincter
options.misconception: None; the sacral reflex pairs detrusor contraction with internal-sphincter relaxation.
options.explanation: Bladder stretch receptors trigger a sacral spinal reflex whose parasympathetic outflow contracts the detrusor muscle and relaxes the involuntary internal urethral sphincter, while somatic motor neurons to the external sphincter are inhibited.

options.label: C
options.text: Cortical inhibition of the sacral micturition center
options.misconception: The learned override is being confused with the reflex itself.
options.explanation: Higher centers delay voiding by holding the external sphincter; the reflex being trained away is the parasympathetic detrusor contraction with sphincter relaxation.

options.label: D
options.text: Stretch-activated contraction of the abdominal wall muscles
options.misconception: A voluntary assist maneuver is being named as the reflex mechanism.
options.explanation: Abdominal contraction can raise intra-abdominal pressure to aid emptying, but the reflex arc itself runs through sacral parasympathetic outflow to the detrusor and internal sphincter.

options.label: E
options.text: Somatic motor outflow contracts the external urethral sphincter
options.misconception: The continence response is being described as the voiding response.
options.explanation: During voiding the spinal cord inhibits the somatic (pudendal) motor neurons, relaxing the skeletal external sphincter; voluntary contraction of that sphincter maintains continence instead.

context: Learning objective: describe the micturition reflex. Sacral stretch reflex → parasympathetic detrusor contraction + internal sphincter relaxation + somatic (pudendal) inhibition of the external sphincter; voluntary control overrides via the external sphincter.
